title: Design System: Exam Prep Design System

brand.purpose: The single chromatic accent; the only hue carrying no verdict meaning.

success.purpose: A correct answer and the mastered segment of a MasteryBar.

warning.purpose: The shaky segment of a MasteryBar and an unresolved fill-in verdict.

display.purpose: Page heroes and marketing headlines only.

mono.purpose: Code, IDs, counts and every compared number; the system's measurement voice.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state and color transitions.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.purpose: The run-progress bar advancing between questions; the system's one authored motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Blanket duration override under prefers-reduced-motion; 0.01ms not 0s so exit transitions still emit transitionend.

components.name: Brand Button
components.description: The single peak action on a surface (Submit, Next question). Never used twice on one screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-brand{font-family:var(--font-sans, system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:.5rem;height:2.25rem;padding:0 .625rem;font-size:.875rem;font-weight:500;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:var(--radius-md, 6px);background:var(--brand, #1f3cf5);color:var(--brand-foreground, #fff);cursor:pointer;transition:background .2s,opacity .2s}.ds-btn-brand:hover{background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand,#1f3cf5) 90%, transparent)}.ds-btn-brand:focus-visible{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring, #1f3cf5) 50%, transparent);}.ds-btn-brand:disabled{opacity:.5;cursor:not-allowed}.ds-btn-brand-kbd{font-family:var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace);font-size:.75rem;opacity:.7}

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ink-filled default action. Every ordinary action on a surface uses this, not the accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary{font-family:var(--font-sans, system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;height:2.25rem;padding:0 .625rem;font-size:.875rem;font-weight:500;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:var(--radius-md, 6px);background:var(--primary, #000);color:var(--primary-foreground, #fff);cursor:pointer;transition:background .2s}.ds-btn-primary:hover{background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary,#000) 80%, transparent)}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring, #1f3cf5) 50%, transparent);}

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Equal-weight choice. Used in pairs where neither option may look preferred — the self-grade Y/N — and for a primary action that is temporarily blocked.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline{font-family:var(--font-sans, system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:.5rem;height:2.5rem;padding:0 .625rem;font-size:.875rem;font-weight:500;border:1px solid var(--border, #e4e4e4);border-radius:var(--radius-md, 6px);background:var(--background, #fcfcfc);color:var(--foreground, #000);cursor:pointer;transition:background .2s,border-color .2s}.ds-btn-outline:hover{background:var(--muted, #f5f5f5)}.ds-btn-outline:focus-visible{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring, #1f3cf5) 50%, transparent);}.ds-btn-outline-kbd{font-family:var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace);font-size:.75rem;color:var(--muted-foreground, #525252)}

components.name: Fill-In Field
components.description: Signature component. Typing the answer from memory is the product thesis, so the unanswered field is the largest, most deliberate element on its surface; once answered it drops to reference scale.
components.css: .ds-fill-in{box-sizing:border-box;font-family:var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace);display:block;width:100%;min-height:3.5rem;padding:.75rem 1rem;font-size:1.25rem;background:var(--card, #fff);color:var(--foreground, #000);border:1px solid var(--input, #ebebeb);border-radius:var(--radius-lg, 8px);caret-color:var(--brand, #1f3cf5);transition:border-color .2s,box-shadow .2s}.ds-fill-in:hover{border-color:color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground,#000) 40%, transparent)}.ds-fill-in:focus{border-color:var(--brand, #1f3cf5);outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring, #1f3cf5) 50%, transparent);}

components.name: Option Key
components.description: Signature component. An answer option's letter is drawn as a key rather than set as a caption, because it is literally the keyboard shortcut that selects it. Selected borrows the accent; answered switches to the verdict colors.

components.name: Wordmark
components.description: No product name has been chosen, so the mark is typographic: the words in the mono face closed by a terminal block cursor. The cursor is the only part of the identity that carries the accent.

components.name: Explanation Well
components.description: A recessed well, not a bordered card: the drill card is already an elevated surface, so a second card on the same ground would be a nested card drawn as a box.
components.html: --usage — most GNU utilities support this "just remind me of the syntax" flag, distinct from the fuller -h.

narrative.overview:
This system is a precision tool, not a personality. It is near-monochrome by intent: black ink on near-white paper (light) and white ink on true black (dark), with color reserved for meaning — the primary action, destruction, answer verdicts, mastery state, and data visualization. The design's job is to make hierarchy, state, and affordance unmistakable using type weight, size, spacing, and hairline borders first, so that the handful of chromatic signals that do exist stay legible instead of competing with decoration.

It explicitly rejects SaaS-template maximalism — purple-to-blue gradients, glassmorphism cards, hero-metric blocks, identical icon-heading-text card grids — and the cream/beige "warm neutral" default. Neutral here is a decision, not an absence.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome; color appears only when it carries meaning (the one peak action, destructive, answer verdict, mastery state, or chart data)
Hierarchy from type weight, size, and whitespace — never from decoration
Hairline borders (#e4e4e4) and whisper-quiet shadows define structure
Every visual value flows from `src/styles/tokens/`; components consume semantic classes (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`) exclusively
Full light/dark parity out of the box

rules.name: The Monochrome Rule
rules.body: Chromatic color is forbidden except: Cobalt for the one peak action, progress, focus and in-progress selection; Signal Red for destruction/errors; Verdict Green/Amber for answer correctness and mastery state; and chart tokens for data visualization. If a screen needs emphasis anywhere else, reach for weight and space, not hue.

rules.name: The One Peak Rule
rules.body: A surface spends the accent once. If two things on a page are cobalt, neither is the peak — demote one to Ink (`default`) or to a bordered/ghost treatment. This is what keeps the accent legible as "the thing to do next" rather than decoration.

rules.name: The Verdict Reservation
rules.body: Green, amber and red belong to answer outcomes and mastery state, and to nothing else. Never reach for them to emphasize an action, and never let the accent stand in for a grade.

rules.name: The Token Door Rule
rules.body: Color enters components only as semantic classes (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`). A raw hex value or Tailwind palette color (`bg-blue-500`) in a component is a defect.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geist carries everything. Introducing a second display face is a per-app branding decision made in `tokens/fonts.css`, never inline.

rules.name: The Row-Reach Rule
rules.body: A row's label and the value it belongs to stay within one comfortable eye-sweep. If a list needs more width than that, the column is too wide — narrow the container rather than stretching the row.

rules.name: More Space Above Than Below
rules.body: A section heading sits closer to the content it introduces than to the section it follows; the rule under a heading binds it downward.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: If a border can express the boundary, use the border. Shadows are reserved for surfaces that genuinely float above the page.

rules.name: The One Line Weight Rule
rules.body: Every border in the system is 1px in the Hairline color. If a boundary needs more emphasis than that, it needs more space or more type weight, not a thicker rule.

dos: Do express every color, radius, shadow, spacing, and font through the token files in `src/styles/tokens/` — that is the only door for visual change.
Do use shadcn semantic classes (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) and built-in `variant` props before any custom styling.
Do ship loading (Skeleton), empty (Empty), error, and disabled states with every surface.
Do keep body text at ≥4.5:1 contrast — Slate Text (#525252) is the lightest allowed body/muted color on light surfaces.

Do rely on `src/styles/tokens/motion.css`'s blanket `prefers-reduced-motion` rule, which already covers every animation by default. Reach for a bespoke crossfade only when an animation carries meaning rather than decoration.
donts: Don't use purple-to-blue gradients, glassmorphism cards, hero-metric blocks, or identical icon-heading-text card grids — the SaaS-template maximalism this system explicitly rejects.
Don't introduce warm cream/beige neutrals; the baseline is near- monochrome by intent, not by omission.
Don't spend the accent twice on one surface, or on anything that is not an action, progress, focus, or an in-progress selection.

Don't stack a page out of identically-bordered cards. A ranked or comparable list is hairline-ruled rows sharing one baseline; a card is for a genuinely distinct navigable object, and never nested inside another card.
Don't write raw hex or Tailwind palette colors (`bg-blue-500`, `text-emerald-600`) in components — semantic tokens only.
Don't use colored side-stripe borders, gradient text, or tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above every section.
Don't nest cards inside cards, or reach for a card when a border or spacing would do.
Don't add decorative charts, badges, or stat tiles that don't answer a user question — dashboard clutter is an anti-reference.
